paragraphs: D-Fend Solutions sells counter-drone systems to military, law enforcement and homeland security agencies. Its core product, EnforceAir, detects a rogue drone, takes control of it through a radio-frequency cyber takeover and brings it to a safe landing. The company describes the approach as non-kinetic and AI-enhanced, built for sensitive and challenging environments.

EnforceAir can operate autonomously or under manual control, and it detects, locates and identifies rogue drones in a protected airspace before taking them over. It is sold in several deployment packages, including a Homeland Security & Law Enforcement Bundle and two tactical configurations, EnforceAir PLUS and EnforceAir2. EnforceAir PLUS, launched in August 2025, adds radar and a jammer to the RF-cyber layer. Beyond agencies, the company says the system has been chosen for large-scale events at stadiums, arenas and open-air venues and for VIP protection.

In an August 2026 press release the company says EnforceAir provided counter-drone security across World Cup host cities and was adopted by more than 20 public safety agencies. Chairman and CEO Zohar Halachmi co-founded the company after founding two mobile and enterprise application start-ups. Its U.S. arm, D-Fend Solutions AD, Inc., is located in McLean, Virginia. In June 2026 the company announced an agreement to be acquired by Motorola Solutions. Its newsroom now states that it has officially joined Motorola Solutions.

quote.text: To truly take full control of a dangerous drone situation, the key is taking control of the drone itself, and staying in control throughout the incident.
